analysis:
Examined: docs/reports/README.md (date bump and one new index link to a mixed-step prefill geometry report; docs-only, no security control or threat-model claim changed), the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump (889fe3c -> f77b384), and SchedulerPrefillBenchmark.swift.

SchedulerPrefillBenchmark.swift is benchmark-only code (ProviderBenchmark target). It bumps the report schema to 5 and adds prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep. It stops recomputing the solo-stripe value separately and instead reads it from the production build's prefillGeometry (head ~157-300). It also adds a guard that every measured engine's geometry equals the warm-up engine's (head ~211-215), and fails closed if a build carries no geometry. There is no new network, crypto, key, attestation, authorization or consumer-data path. It does not touch the coordinator WebSocket contract, App Attest, the SSD prefix cache or T-041 surfaces. Benchmark prompts are synthetic seed text. The change improves receipt integrity and does not weaken any threat-model mitigation.

Limits: the submodule bump (libs/mlx-swift-lm) shows only a commit hash change, so its actual content is not visible and cannot be assessed. The submodule likely supplies the new EngineV2Factory.PrefillGeometry and prefillGeometry fields. It may also change Gemma 4 prompt geometry (2,048/4,096 prefill and media ceilings per the README text), which could affect TB-007 inference-engine memory/activation behavior (T-028, T-029, T-041), but nothing in the supplied evidence establishes a regression. Also unseen are the factory-side implementation of makeProductionBuild and the prefillGeometry type, which are outside the supplied patch. The next pass should review the submodule diff if available, including any change to prefill chunking, KV/cache keying or SSD cache gating (T-041 detection hints), and media size ceilings.
